Add the PHW footer (logo and source) to a ggplot

Source: R/ggplot.R
phw_finalise.Rd

Adds a branded footer under a chart: a thin navy rule, the PHW logo on one side and the source text on the other. Use it for charts that stand alone, such as slides, social media, briefings or images sent by email. Charts inside a branded report don't need it, because the report already carries the logo.

Usage

phw_finalise(
  plot,
  source = NULL,
  date = NULL,
  logo = "blue",
  team = NULL,
  logo_height = 1.1,
  logo_position = c("left", "right"),
  text_size = 8.5,
  text_colour = phw_colours[["text"]],
  rule_colour = phw_colours[["navy"]],
  rule = TRUE,
  margin = 4,
  ...
)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot, a patchwork (e.g. from phw_arrange()), a cowplot figure, or any grob or gtable (e.g. from gridExtra::arrangeGrob()).

source, date

Passed to phw_caption(). Leave both NULL to keep any caption already on the plot.

logo

Logo variant (see phw_logo()), a path to your own PNG, or FALSE for none.

team

Optional line under the source, e.g. "Communicable Disease Surveillance Centre".

logo_height

Logo height in cm.

logo_position

"left" or "right". The text goes on the other side.

text_size

Footer text size in points.

text_colour, rule_colour

Colours of the footer text and rule.

rule

Draw the rule above the footer?

margin

Space at each side, in mm.

...

Passed to phw_caption(), e.g. source_prefix = "Data: " or note = "Provisional".

Value

A gtable that prints like a plot. Save it with phw_save().

Examples

library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Weight and fuel economy", x = "Weight (1,000 lbs)",
       y = "Miles per gallon")

# Source and date under the chart, with the logo if you have one
# (see phw_download_logos()); otherwise the organisation name is shown.
fp <- phw_finalise(p, source = "mtcars", date = as.Date("2025-06-30"))
phw_save(fp, tempfile(fileext = ".png"))

# A team line, and no logo
fp <- phw_finalise(p, source = "mtcars", team = "Team name", logo = FALSE)
